claims.explanation: Prednisolone's selective killing is most plausibly driven by glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1)-mediated transcriptional activation of pro-apoptotic and anti-proliferative genes, with sensitivity determined by intact GR signaling and an apoptotic-competent background. Lines with TP53 mutations and/or PI3K-pathway activation (PIK3CA, PTEN loss) appear enriched among sensitive lines, while EGFR/MAPK-driven lung and BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are relatively resistant, suggesting that active RTK/RAS/MAPK signaling and possibly mutant EGFR protect from glucocorticoid-induced apoptosis. NR3C1 expression and downstream GR target induction (e.g., TSC22D3) are the key predictors of response.

features.basis: GR is the annotated target; response requires receptor expression and intact signaling
TP53 mutations are highly enriched in the most-killed lines, consistent with impaired DNA-damage/apoptotic checkpoints lowering the threshold for glucocorticoid-induced death
PIK3CA mutations appear in several sensitive lines (SNU840, HGC27, MKN1, SNUC5), suggesting PI3K activation cooperates with GR-driven apoptosis
PTEN loss (ZR751) is observed among sensitive lines and may enhance glucocorticoid-induced apoptosis via unrestrained PI3K/AKT signaling
EGFR-mutant lung lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven survival signaling antagonizes GR-induced apoptosis
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (IGR37, UACC62, IPC298) are relatively resistant, consistent with MAPK pathway activation promoting survival
KRAS-mutant lines appear in both groups but several resistant lines (T3M4, NCIH1437 via MAP2K1) have RAS/MAPK activation, suggesting mutant KRAS may blunt glucocorticoid response
GILZ (TSC22D3) is strongly induced by prednisolone in the virtual cell and is a canonical GR target mediating anti-proliferative/apoptotic effects
NFKBIA induction by prednisolone in the virtual cell indicates GR-mediated NF-kB inhibition, which can sensitize cells to apoptosis
Survivin (BIRC5) is downregulated by prednisolone in the virtual cell; high baseline BIRC5 expression would be expected to protect from apoptosis
CDKN2A loss appears in several sensitive lines (SNU1214, MHHES1, K029AX, IPC298), suggesting cell-cycle deregulation enhances glucocorticoid-induced growth arrest/apoptosis
ATM mutations appear in sensitive lines (SNU685, SNUC5), consistent with defective DNA-damage responses lowering the apoptotic threshold
